Chapter 6: Learning to Live in the In-Between
You know that strange, almost itchy feeling you get when you’re stuck between what used to be, and what’s not quite here yet?
That’s the in-between—the liminal space where you’re neither fully in the past nor firmly rooted in your future. Most of us? We get restless. We just want to fast-forward through this part, craving answers and resolution. But let’s be honest—life doesn’t always follow the timeline we hope for.
Picture this: A woman steps away from a job she’s had for years. Suddenly, the daily routines that gave her life structure just vanish. The future? It looks like a blank page, and that emptiness can feel overwhelming. She tries to fill it—with new projects, big plans, anything to make the waiting feel useful. But nothing really sticks; it’s like trying to hold onto water.
Friends chime in with advice—“Take a class! Start something new! Volunteer!”—all with good intentions. But none of it feels quite right. Eventually, she lets go of the urge to force a solution. She gives herself permission to just be. Long walks, a stack of novels, a hot mug between her hands—these small comforts start to fill her days.
And in that quiet space, something shifts. She begins to notice little things: the way sunlight drifts across the floor, the soothing sound of rain tapping at the window, or simply the peace of a slow morning. It’s here she realizes—the in-between isn’t wasted time.
It’s actually a season where new ideas and new parts of ourselves are quietly taking root, even if we can’t see them just yet. Most people miss this, rushing ahead, desperate to feel settled again. But there’s real wisdom in waiting. Sure, the discomfort is real. But so is the possibility.
Sometimes, it’s only in the stillness that new dreams begin to take shape. Dreams you might’ve missed if you’d hurried on too quickly.
So, learning to live in the in-between? It’s all about patience and trust. It’s daring to sit with the uncertainty and resisting that urge to fill every silence with noise. Over time, you might notice the anxiety fading, replaced by a gentle curiosity—wondering what’s just around the corner.
Suddenly, the in-between stops feeling like a place of loss. Instead, it’s a space filled with possibility—waiting quietly for whatever comes next.
